# tools

Tool registry, permission-gated execution and context-bomb guard.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-tools.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-tools.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** nothing
- **Required by:** [agent](agent.md), [perms](perms.md), [readonly](readonly.md), [skills](skills.md), [supervisor](supervisor.md), [tool-slots](tool-slots.md), [tools-agent](tools-agent.md), [tools-compact](tools-compact.md), [tools-dev](tools-dev.md), [tools-emacs](tools-emacs.md), [tools-emacs-eval](tools-emacs-eval.md), [tools-events](tools-events.md), [tools-fs](tools-fs.md), [tools-handin](tools-handin.md), [tools-notify](tools-notify.md), [tools-plan](tools-plan.md), [tools-question](tools-question.md), [tools-session-info](tools-session-info.md), [tools-sessions](tools-sessions.md), [tools-shell](tools-shell.md), [tools-ssh](tools-ssh.md), [tools-todo](tools-todo.md), [tools-web](tools-web.md)

## About

Tools are declared with `harness-define-tool` and executed with the
`tools/execute` method, which runs the permission chain, the handler
(with a timeout), the context-bomb guard and the result filter.  A
tool never runs without a permission decision; when no permission
module is installed every call is denied, so a misconfigured harness
fails safe.

A tool has two names: NAME, the identifier the model calls it by
(read_file), and its `:label`, the name people read (Read file),
which every UI shows in its place.  A call's title is the label,
then what the call is about, from the tool's `:subject` function:
"Read file: src/x.el".

Some providers have tools of their own that can stand in for a
harness tool: Claude Code's web search for web_search, say.  A
provider names the harness tools it has such a counterpart of in its
`:builtin-tools` capability, and `tools/builtin` says which of them a
session's provider runs itself; `tools/list` then leaves them out.
The calls the provider runs still need a permission decision, which
`tools/authorize` gives without running anything.

What a tool prints is filtered before anything keeps it.  The result
goes through the `tools/output` filter first (value: the RESULT, then
the session id and the call), ahead of the size guard, so that the
file an oversized result is saved to holds what the filter let
through, not the raw text; then through the guard, then the
`tools/result` filter.  The secrets module is the `tools/output`
filter that takes secrets out of `:content` (and says so in the
result's `:meta`).  The text a tool reports as progress or as a note
goes through `tools/output-text` (value: the text, then the session
id) before it is announced, and so does the output the harness
records for a call a provider ran itself, so every route a tool's
text takes to a transcript, a UI or a model passes a filter.

Corporate mode (`harness-corporate-mode`) turns off the tools of kind
net other than web search (`harness-tools--corporate-net-tools`),
and ssh, which runs commands on other machines
(`harness-tools--corporate-remote-tools`).  No session gets them,
and a call to one is refused before the permission chain, whatever
the permission mode and the standing rules say
(`harness-tools--corporate-refusal`).  web_search stays, and so does
a provider's own search in its place: that is a call of web_search
too, which the permission chain decides as usual.

Every tool reaches another host through TRAMP, given a path there or
in a session on that host.  A call that fails because TRAMP could not
connect says why and how to set the host up, whichever tool made it
(`harness-tools-remote-failure`).

## Provides

### Methods

- `tools/authorize` (session-id call) — Decide whether CALL (:id :name :input :kind) of SESSION-ID may run.
- `tools/builtin` (session-id) — Return the names of the harness tools that SESSION-ID's provider runs itself.
- `tools/execute` (session-id call) — Execute CALL (:id :name :input) for SESSION-ID; return a promise of a RESULT.
- `tools/execute-approved` (session-id call) — Run CALL (:id :name :input) for SESSION-ID with no permission check.
- `tools/get` (name) — Return the spec of tool NAME or nil.
- `tools/list` (&optional session-id) — Return tool specs available to SESSION-ID (or all), after `agent/tools`.

### Events

- `permission/decided` — (SESSION-ID REQUEST DECISION) after the permission chain.
- `tools/file-written` — (PATH) after a tool wrote PATH; the UI reverts buffers visiting it.
- `tools/finished` — (SESSION-ID CALL RESULT) after execution or denial.
- `tools/note` — (SESSION-ID CALL-ID TEXT) what a running tool shows under its call: a line or a few for people to read, which the agent keeps on the call and the chat draws (see `harness-tools-watch-session`).
- `tools/progress` — (SESSION-ID CALL-ID TEXT) progress from a running tool.
- `tools/started` — (SESSION-ID CALL) before permission and execution.

### Filter chains it runs

- `agent/builtin-tools`
- `agent/tools`
- `permission/decide`
- `tools/output`
- `tools/output-text`
- `tools/result`

### Options

- `harness-tools-max-output-chars` — Tool outputs longer than this are saved to a file and truncated.
